the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of the function of the glutamate receptors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phosphorylation targets the functional coupling of glutamate channels.
phosphorylation of AMPA receptors is not a mechanism for the long-term modulation of synaptic strength.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phosphorylation of the GluR1 subunit of the AMPA receptor causes the receptor to become more sensitive to glutamate.
the phosphorylation of the NMDA receptor by PKA causes a change in the affinity of the receptor to glutamate and glycine, without changing the intrinsic gating of the channel itself.
glutamate receptor function can be modulated by phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phosphorylation of AMPA receptors is an important mechanism for controlling the functional coupling between glutamate binding and channel gating (Traynelis & Cull-Candy, 1990; Traynelis et al. 1995).
glutamate receptors can undergo a long-lasting change in their functional behaviour.
the gating of glutamate channels can be regulated by the phosphorylation of the channel protein.
